segments.text: "Welcome to 'Gear Up', the daily robotics news digest, August 19th, 2026.
We've got the latest on the first paid robot rental, a bipedal humanoid making its WRC debut, and AI advancements in ROS.
Your daily dose of robotics news, right here."
From Robotics & Automation News, "Faraday Future’s RoboShare takes first paid robot rental order."

Faraday Future Intelligent Electric's (FFAI) support for AIxC Holdings' orderly exit from its digital asset treasury strategy has led to the completion of AIxC's first paid commercial order, marking the platform's transition into commercial operations and initial revenue generation.

This was accomplished through the provision of customized performance production and content design services for Los Angeles-based artist DU$TY, with the platform set to expand its product offerings and develop the market.

FFAI will provide AIxC with strategic, product, technology, business, and capital-market support to help the company establish a sustainable business model centered on transaction and service revenue.
This milestone signals the platform's growth and sets a precedent for future commercial collaborations.
From Humanoids Daily, "Galbot Teases ET1 Bipedal Humanoid Ahead of WRC 2026 Debut,"
Galbot, a Beijing-based robotics startup, has previewed its fully bipedal humanoid robot, the ET1, ahead of its formal debut at WRC 2026 in Beijing.
The ET1 showcases dynamic athletic capabilities through a CGI teaser, highlighting its ability to swing a tennis racket, demonstrating a significant advancement in bipedal locomotion.
The robot is based on the LATENT athletic framework, which was introduced earlier this year and validated on a third-party platform, marking a significant milestone in the humanoid sector.
Galbot's expansion into bipedal locomotion reflects the intensifying competitive pressure in the humanoid sector, with the company eyeing a potential $4 billion IPO.
The company's move is expected to further accelerate innovation in humanoid robotics.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Foxglove has agents now".

Foxglove has introduced several new features, including a search experience that allows querying recordings with combined topic and semantic search, an A/B comparison feature for visualizing and comparing robot runs, an agent sidebar that enables tasks such as creating layouts and triaging issues, and improvements to remote access and Bring Your Own Server (BYOS) functionality, including optimized WebRTC streams and the ability to use a single storage bucket.
These enhancements aim to simplify and streamline the user experience, providing a more efficient and effective workflow for developers and users.
By implementing these features, Foxglove is further solidifying its position as a leader in the ROS ecosystem.
From Humanoids Daily, "Unitree Soars Over 600% in Shanghai IPO, Cements China’s Lead in Humanoid Hardware".
Unitree Robotics, a Chinese hardware manufacturer, has made its highly anticipated IPO on the Shanghai STAR Market, with its shares skyrocketing by up to 629%.
The company's IPO marks a significant milestone in its growth trajectory, showcasing its exceptional vertical integration capabilities.
Unitree produces 86% of its bill of materials in-house, allowing for streamlined production and reduced reliance on external suppliers.
Strategic partnerships have also been secured to tackle industry software bottlenecks, further bolstering the company's competitive edge.
This impressive feat underscores China's dominance in the humanoid hardware sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Scientists combine EIT and pneumatic sensing for humanoid robot skin."
Scientists have developed a hybrid robotic skin combining electrical impedance tomography and pneumatic pressure sensing to improve force detection across large areas of a humanoid robot.
The system uses EIT to determine where contact occurs, while four sealed pneumatic pads provide an estimate of the force being applied.
The researchers report a significant reduction in sensitivity variation, with the coefficient of variation falling from 0.31 to 0.14.
The approach takes advantage of the different strengths of the two technologies, allowing EIT to provide spatial information while pneumatic sensing provides a net-force measurement.
This new hybrid system is a breakthrough in the development of more advanced and reliable humanoid robots.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Hexagon starts training AEON humanoid robots at Schaeffler factories."

Hexagon Robotics and Schaeffler have announced a significant collaboration, with AEON humanoid robots now training at Schaeffler's Humanoid Gym in Germany, a dedicated industrial environment designed to support AEON's learning and validation.
The training program utilizes imitation learning and repeated execution, allowing AEON to acquire new industrial tasks and improve its performance.
Schaeffler will provide advanced actuator technology to AEON, enabling its industrial deployment across its manufacturing operations.
The training program aims to accelerate AEON's deployment across multiple use cases in manufacturing workflows within the next six months.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Opinion: How robots are learning to navigate the building site".
Autonomous robots are being tested on construction sites to improve navigation without relying on GPS.

A recent deployment at a construction site in Oxford has successfully mapped the site and carried out autonomous inspection within four hours using Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping (SLAM) technology, which utilizes LiDAR to build a map in real-time.
The technology addresses the "where am I" and "what does this space look like" problems.
However, the technology faces limitations, including issues with airborne dust and physical debris, as well as deployment cost and integration with existing site management software.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Rodriguez launches Movotrak ‘seventh axis’ for cobots"
, Rodriguez has introduced the Movotrak Cobot Transfer Unit, allowing a cobot to move between multiple workstations, extending its operating range to up to 10 meters.

The system incorporates integrated collision detection, which enables the carriage to automatically stop in case of a collision, thereby increasing robot utilisation and reducing changeover requirements.
The system is designed to be compatible with standard cobots and can be installed horizontally or mounted on a wall or ceiling, providing flexibility in its deployment.
From Robotics & Automation News, "VUB leads European project teaching soft robots to sense, repair and adapt,"
a four-year European research project called RESSORT has been launched, aiming to make soft robots more sustainable, intelligent, and reliable.
Vrije Universiteit Brussel leads the project, combining breakthrough technologies such as self-healing materials, variable-stiffness structures, and advanced multi-material 3D printing techniques.

Researchers will develop demonstrators, including a personalized soft exosuit for healthcare, an adaptive robotic system for the food industry, and a deformable drone for inspection tasks in confined environments.
The project's partners, including 13 other countries, will collaborate to advance the field of soft robotics.
The RESSORT project is funded by the European Union's Horizon Europe research and innovation programme.
From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Autonomous drones and the future of war in an AI-driven world | Letter,"
the article highlights the significant risk posed by autonomous drones to civilians, as these machines that kill without distinction leave no one safe.
According to experts, the principle of distinction, which requires a gap between a target and a lawful target, is difficult to close with autonomous drones.
The letter argues that if the laws of war cannot be programmed into drones, a greater intelligence cannot be trusted with our values.
The letter emphasizes that the lack of accountability and oversight in autonomous drone warfare systems threatens the very fabric of international law.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Warehouse robotics company Brightpick expands partnership with Dr. Max Group,"
Brightpick, a provider of AI-powered warehouse automation, is expanding its partnership with Dr.

Max Group, Europe's largest pharmacy chain, by deploying 44 additional autonomous mobile robots across facilities in the Czech Republic and Slovakia, bringing the total number of deployed robots to 74 units.
The partnership has led to a significant reduction in manual picking labor and an increase in warehouse capacity, with a 95% decrease in manual picking labor and a 40% increase in warehouse capacity.
The expanded partnership includes new projects in the Czech Republic and Slovakia, further solidifying Brightpick's position in the AI-powered warehouse automation market.
From Robotics & Automation News, "A3 and Mahoning County expand access to free robotics training in Ohio through $500,000 workforce grant".
A3 and Mahoning County Career & Technical Center have announced plans to offer no-cost robotics and automation training to Ohio residents through a $499,000 workforce grant.

The training program, which is available online, will cover industry-recognized topics and cater to a diverse range of learners, including students, educators, adult learners, and manufacturing employers.
The program aims to help small and medium-sized manufacturers develop a skilled workforce to effectively adopt robotics and automation technologies.
The training will be made available through a partnership with Automate, a leading industry organization.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: ROS Keeps Evolving via Physical AI SIG".

Researchers at OSRA, in collaboration with the Special Interest Group on Physical AI, have published a blog post detailing their efforts to integrate Physical AI with ROS, proposing that leveraging the strengths of both is the most effective path forward, resulting in a more robust and versatile AI framework.

Researchers at OSRA and the SIG PAI have made significant strides in exploring the potential of integrating Physical AI with ROS, publishing a comprehensive blog post that outlines their methodology and findings.
By leveraging the strengths of both, the team has proposed a more streamlined approach to AI development, allowing for faster and more efficient integration of physical and digital AI systems.
The group's ongoing work is focused on developing a robust framework for integrating Physical AI with ROS, with a long-term roadmap that aims to achieve this integration in the near future.
This collaboration between OSRA and the SIG PAI has significant implications for the AI and tech industry, as it paves the way for the development of more sophisticated and integrated AI systems.

As the Physical AI SIG continues to explore the potential of this integration, it is likely that we will see more innovative applications and developments in the field, further advancing the capabilities of ROS and the broader AI community.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Drones With Claws Perch on Arctic Icebergs,"
researchers have developed a drone called Ice Dart that is capable of perching on glaciers and drifting icebergs.
The drone features shock-absorbing legs and spiny feet that enable it to latch onto the ice, allowing for long-term monitoring of these areas.
The process was accomplished by employing a robotic system that utilizes a combination of robotic arms and hydraulic actuators to control the drone's movements and stabilize its footing.
The methodology involved the use of advanced computer algorithms and sensor integration to ensure precise navigation and balance.
The key result of this achievement is the successful deployment of the Ice Dart drone on the Arctic icebergs, paving the way for more precise and extensive monitoring of these regions.

That's a spark of excitement we can't ignore.
Until tomorrow's circuit break, warmely yours!"
